challenges.title: Partitions, consumer groups and lag
challenges.prompt: Model a topic with key-based partitioning and a consumer group: assignment() gives each partition to exactly one member (round-robin), poll() reads from the committed offset, commit() advances offsets and lag() reports end minus committed per partition. Check the rebalance with more members than partitions.
challenges.explain: Each partition is owned by one member of the group, offsets are committed per partition and lag is end offset minus committed offset; extra members get no partitions. This is a teaching model, not the Kafka client. Verified by running the solution.

challenges.title: Idempotent producer and at-least-once consumer
challenges.prompt: Complete Broker.append (dedupe by (producer, sequence) when enabled) and Consumer.run (process then commit; a crash before commit means the record is processed again). Compare plain retries with idempotence, and a naive consumer with an idempotent handler.
challenges.expected:
plain retries -> ['a', 'b', 'b', 'b', 'c']
idempotence -> ['a', 'b', 'c']
crashed ['a', 'b'] committed 1
done ['a', 'b', 'b', 'c'] committed 3
side effects by key (naive): {'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 1}
applied with idempotent handler: ['a', 'b', 'c']
challenges.explain: Sequence numbers let the broker drop duplicate retries, while commit-after-processing gives at-least-once delivery, so side effects must be idempotent. Verified by running the solution.
